title: urgent: investigate & remediate multi-deployment token-rate collapse during model fanout
creator: Liam Chen
description: Customer-reported widespread first-token latency (TTFT) spikes and sustained tokens/sec drop across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments when requests fan out to multimodel variants. Incident started after a rolling change to the request router and kernel warmup heuristics. Customers reported 3x increase in TTFT and degraded throughput for Llama2-13B and Mistral-7B variants.
impact_summary: Multiple enterprise customers on Dedicated and several Hosted tenants observed TTFT increase from ~120ms to ~400ms and a tokens/sec drop of 50-70% under typical traffic patterns. Several SLAs were breached for a subset of dedicated customers; engineering paged and engaged on-call within 12 minutes of first escalation.

investigation_findings: Regression introduced by scheduler rollout that changed fanout ordering and early prefetch thresholds
Kernel warmup heuristics interacted poorly with quantized execution path causing repeated kernel-select thrash during concurrent fanout
KV cache eviction policy had a bug when fanout depth > 3 that evicted priming prefixes prematurely, forcing repeated warmups
Under moderate concurrency the router induced uneven microbatching causing some workers to fall behind and trigger backpressure loops
root_cause: A combined regression: scheduler reordering + too-aggressive KV eviction for deep fanout triggered kernel warmup churn. This increased priming work and reduced effective tokens/sec; subsequent microbatch imbalance amplified the effect under multi-tenant load.
actions_taken: Immediate rollback of scheduler reorder in canary and hold of global rollout
Emergency hotfix: increased KV-prefetch window, fixed eviction condition for fanout > 3, and disabled quant-kernel autoprobing during steady-state traffic
Added temporary per-tenant concurrency cap for affected dedicated clusters to prevent SLA breach escalations
Deployed targeted drain-and-warmup to persistent workers to repopulate KV caches for high-fanout customers
Created dedicated dashboard slices and synthetic tests for fanout depth scenarios

monitoring_and_alerting_changes: Added new alert for TTFT delta > 150ms specifically correlated with fanout_depth >= 4
Synthetic job added: multi-model fanout depth sweep (0..6) with token-rate and TTFT metrics every 5m
Adjusted existing prefetch telemetry to report eviction counts per-request-label
postmortem_actions: Ship deterministic fix for eviction bug and scheduler interaction (runtime-1.22.4)
Introduce unit/integration tests that simulate deep-fanout KV lifecycles
Improve deployment gate: require fanout-depth regression test for scheduler rollouts
Add canary with higher concurrency diversity to catch microbatch imbalance regressions
Schedule cross-team review with Kernel, Router, and Runtime owners to tighten rollout coordination
resolution_summary: Hotfix v1 addressed the immediate tokens/sec regression by stopping premature KV evictions and rolling back scheduler reordering. After the patch, TTFT and tokens/sec returned to within 10-15% of baseline for most customers; a deterministic code fix is in progress and targeted for runtime-1.22.4. Monitoring and a customer validation window are in place.
